newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - Feb 14.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - Feb 14.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Property group Lend Lease has stepped up its aggressive push to secure new construction business by joining casino operator Hudson Conway to bid for the A$2 billion Melbourne Docklands development. However major competitor Thiess Contractors upped the stakes announcing it had formed an alliance with three offshore groups to bid for the project. Page 1.

The continued strength of Wall Street, the unexpectedly good interim profits and recent buying by domestic and foreign investors have led the Australian sharemarket to another record high yesterday, with leading investment managers expecting the momentum to carry the market even higher. The All Ordinaries Index broke 2500 at one stage yesterday, eventually closing 22.9 points above opening at 2496.4. Page 1.

Former Coles Myer chairman and chief executive Brian Quinn goes on trial on Monday, charged with conspiring to defraud the retail giant. The case involves allegations about a series of renovations carried out at the Quinn residence. Page 3.

Fairfax shareholders will vote at a meeting next Friday on whether New Zealand's Brierley Investments Ltd should be allowed to move from 20 per cent to 25 per cent ownership of the company without making a takeover bid. AMP Investment's head of marketable securities, Merv Peacock has said AMP will vote 'no' on the issue, with Bankers Trust and Axiom Funds Management set to join them. Page 33.

Australian property and financial services group Lend Lease posted a strong increase in net profit to A$160 million for the half year to last December, marking a rise of 14.2 per cent over the 1995 half. Directors declared a fully franked dividend of 48cents a share, up from 43 cents. Page 33.

Following a 2.7 per cent fall in net profit for the December half, printer, publisher and multi-media company PMP Communications Ltd is looking for a boost from cost cutting and cheaper paper prices. Last year's A$174.3 million acquisition of graphic art and CD manufacturer, Shomega boosted PMP sales by 22 per cent to A$589 million, as the company yesterday reported net earnings of A$30.5 million for the half after a goodwill amortisation expense of $3.6 million. Page 34.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Petroz NL shares moved to a 10-year high yesterday following the company's announcement of a new discovery in the Timor Sea which would add to the reserves of its Elang-Kakatua oil field. The groups shares jumped 12 cents to A$1.12, or 12 per cent, within minutes of the announcement to the market. Page 21.

The appetite for Australian shares continued yesterday with the All Ordinaries Index moving to a record high. The indicator briefly broke the 2500-point mark before closing 22.9 points higher at 2496.4. Overall this represents a 400 point gain to the Austalian market over the past seven months. Page 21.

The Commonwealth Bank has announced plans to expand into Asia and New Zealand and into the area of funds management. Revealing a half-year profit of A$602 million, Commonwealth's managing director said the expansion would be achieved through takeovers or joint ventures. Page 21.

At least four signatures have been put on paper in the north-western Queensland town Mt Isa, which is hosting native title negotiations over the A$1.1 billion Century Zinc project. The signatures are on an agreement thrashed out between 12 indigenous landholders, mining giant CRA and the Qld Government. The Native Title Tribunal's Rick Farley says the four other claimants are in Mount Isa and are being contacted by phone and fax in an attempt to secure their signatures. Page 21.

A report commissioned by the Australian Information Industry Association, the Australian Telecommunications Users Group and a information services provider network has warned that Australia could still revert to a Telstra monopoly, despite massive legislation which aims to deregulate the telecommunications industry after July 1. Page 23.

According to analysts, Pacific Dunlop Ltd's board and management will have to post an interim net profit of more than A$90 million before abnormals to avoid the prospect of a takeover bid. In its first half-year since the introduction of new management and the divestiture of more than A$1.8 billion of non-core assets, the new changes will have to bear fruit for the company to avoid a break-up. Page 23.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Property giant Lend Lease is on track for its 19th consecutive record profit following yesterday's announcement of a A$160 million half year profit. The 14 per cent increase in the December half earnings was accentuated by growth in financial services and a stronger property market. Page 25.

Retail property managers, the Westfield Group, has submitted a proposal for the amalgamation and expansion of its two Hornsby shopping centres, north-west of Sydney, to create one of Australia's largest retail complexes with an estimated value of A$450 million. Page 25.

Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting will move behind Brierley Investments purchase of a further 4.9 per cent of newspaper publisher John Fairfax Holdings at next week's extraordinary general meeting. It is believed that PBL supports the proposal to ensure Brierley secures what is now a 24.9 per cent stake in Fairfax immediately. Page 25.

Commonwealth Bank's managing director, David Murray, has outlined details of planned aggressive expansion. The plan includes joint ventures in select Asian countries and the acquisition of financial service providers in New Zealand. Page 27.

The Australian Broadcasting Corporation has ruled out an attempt by three staff of Australia Television of a management buyout plan for the satellite service. ABC management informed the hopefuls that the internal consortium would not be considered as it could be seen as having an unfair advantage over other bidders. Page 27.

The Australian sharemarket broke through the 2500 mark for the first time yesterday following strong global sharemarket results. The All Ordinaries index reached a high of 2500.9 during the day, but later shifted down to close 22.9 points ahead at 2496.4. Page 28.
THE AGE

Two of the most powerful bidders for the A$2 billion Melbourne Docklands project - Hudson Conway and Lend Lease - yesterday joined forces in what is believed to be an even split. Hudson Conway chief executive Lloyd Williams believed the combination of the two companies would greatly enhance the prospects for a successful tender. Page C1.

More details of the Commonwealth Bank's aggressive expansion plans were revealed yesterday by managing director David Murray. Murray identified joint ventures in select Asian countries, and acquisitions of financial service providers in New Zealand as high on the agenda, with the acquisitions centred around boosting the bank's non-core financial service and investment banking businesses. Page C1.

The All Ordinaries Index achieved a second consecutive record close yesterday, as world sharemarkets continued their dizzying climb, with turnover reaching almost A$1.4 billion after being stimulated by another record-breaking performance by Wall Street and encouraging local job statistics. 556.2 million shares were traded and the Share Price Index rose 20 points to finish on 2501. Page C1.

Japanese company Fujii-Keori, one of the world's biggest buyers of superfine wool, yesterday urged the Australian Government and the wool industry to spend more promoting the fibre as a fashion item. Fujii-Keori president Kemroku Fujii criticised the complex web of wool organisations in Australia, and said not enough was being done to promote the product and boost customer demand. Page C1.

Next Friday's meeting of Fairfax shareholders will see Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting throw its weight behind New Zealand's Brierley Investment's push to move from 20 to 25 per cent ownership. The approval given by PBL contrasts the negative responses to the proposal from Fairfax's other key shareholder, Bankers Trust. Page C3.

Concerns are growing about publishing group Rural Press's hopes for profit growth following a decline for the first few weeks of 1997 caused by difficult economic conditions. Rural Press chairman John Fairfax said he still hoped to maintain the company's history of profit, and analysts were cheered by 4.2 per cent rise in net profits for the six months to December 31. Page C3.

Placer Pacific is expected to record static or slightly lower results for gold mining concern this year, following rising costs and a fall in gold production, as its 1996 net profit was confirmed yesterday at A$43.52 million - down by 26 per cent. Placer said the increased cost of sales, interest expense, depreciation, amortisation and a decline in other income more than offset the 15.8 per cent rise in sales. Page C3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
